title: Right-argument shift comparison for internal derived Hom
statement: On a small ringed site (C,R), with the unbounded derived category D(R) and the internal derived Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], fix P in D(R) and n in Z. Write F_P(Q)=RHom(P,Q), with morphisms RHom(id_P,q). There is a natural isomorphism F_P followed by shift(n) to shift(n) followed by F_P. No boundedness or K-flatness is assumed.

source.place: Sections 21.34 and 21.35, Hom-complex differential and representative computation (Tags 0A8X and 08JA); signed shift calculation in step 2 of lem-sc-global-hom-shifted-hypercohomology

proof.text: Represent P by L and Q by a functorial K-injective I. The shifted I[n] is K-injective: an acyclic test complex shifted by -n is acyclic, and the shift equivalence transports null-homotopies.

In degree k, identify Hom(L,I)[n]^k and Hom(L,I[n])^k by the identity on their factors Hom(L^p,I^(p+k+n)). Both differentials have postcomposition coefficient (-1)^n and precomposition coefficient -(-1)^k, so this identification is a chain isomorphism. It and its inverse commute with postcomposition.

Localize the chain isomorphism and use representative comparisons to compute RHom(P,Q[n]) with I[n]. Quasi-isomorphism invariance makes the comparison independent of representatives. Derived morphisms between K-injective representatives are chain maps modulo homotopy, and the component comparison commutes with both chain maps and homotopies. Thus it gives the required natural isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Sections 21.34 and 21.35: one-variable specialization of the signed shift calculation in lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-comparison

Derived internal Hom shift in first or second argument natural isomorphism
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results: generic derived functor CommShift, ShiftedHom.opEquiv, and HomComplex shift APIs. None is a shift comparison of the sheaf-valued internal Hom.
Generic shiftFunctorCompIsoId API. Read shiftFunctorAdd and shiftFunctorAdd' in Shift.Basic; these combine shifts but supply no internal Hom comparison.
Only ordinary HomComplex cochains and generic shift APIs. DerivedInternalHom has representative comparisons but no shift theorem. The simultaneous shift comparison is the parent being reduced.

from.place: Right-argument part of the signed shift comparison

lean.statement:
theorem derivedInternalHom_shift_right
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R))]
    (P : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R))) (n : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (
      ((Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHom.{u, w} (C := C) J R)).obj (op P) ⋙
        shiftFunctor _ (n)) ≅
      (shiftFunctor _ n ⋙
        (Functor.curry.obj (derivedInternalHom.{u, w} (C := C) J R)).obj (op P)))
